reviews.title: A generous promise, quietly taken back
reviews.text:
During COVID, Down Dog generously offered free memberships to first responders and teachers. I was genuinely grateful and, because I believed that access would continue, I chose not to buy the lifetime membership they were offering at the time.

Then the lifetime option disappeared, and shortly afterward, the free memberships were quietly revoked.

That sequence left a lasting impression on me. What had felt like an act of goodwill ended up feeling temporary in a way that materially affected a purchasing decision I can no longer make.

I would have happily supported this company. Instead, years later, I still refuse to subscribe. Trust is easy to earn with a generous gesture; it is much harder to rebuild once that gesture is taken back.

reviews.title: Long time subscriber, cancelling
reviews.text: I have subscribed to this app since 2023, but have noted the quality of the auto-generated flows declining. An 80 minute vinyasa beginner 2 program was 45 minutes (huh?) and half an abs workout (dead bugs and crunches?) with terrible pose transitions (nonexistent.) This app served me well for a long time, but is not suitable for anyone serious about their practice.

reviews.title: Restore the direct download button
reviews.text: Please restore the direct download button for online practices. In older versions, I could download a practice as I started it, but now I have to create offline practices separately. This makes it hard to repeat specific yoga flows I enjoy when I do not have internet, and it's been a disappointing change.

reviews.title: I do not recommend this yoga app.
reviews.text: I don’t recommend this app for the simple fact that it does not listen. I’ve been using it for two months and it’s stretched only my hips. No matter how much I have tried to program stretches that target the arms and chest and shoulders, this app gives nothing but hips and quads. In a 30 min practice with chest and shoulders as the focus we did zero chest or shoulder stretches, hips and quads only. So then I programmed a 5 min only chest and shoulders and it did one stretches for my triceps and then straight back to a quad stretch for the remainder of the practice. Use a different app that will actually listen to you and your body, not whatever it wants.

reviews.title: Not good for beginners!
reviews.text: I have returned to yoga after a long hiatus and this had great reviews, however even on the beginner level 1 setting I found some of the moves utterly mental. Who on earth is able to do a chateranga at beginner level?! I also seem to be spending a vast portion of my time upside down which makes me feel quite sick. I’m going back to Les Mills I think. Love the feature of a different workout every time but it’s a waste of money for me as mostly I sit on the mat trying to figure out in which reality this is suited to beginners.
